title: The Six-Minute Walk Test — Measuring Breathlessness Safely

hook.en: Walking for six minutes tells you more about a patient's daily life than many lab tests. Learn to run the test exactly the same way every time, watch the oxygen level and breathlessness, and know when to stop.
hook.ur: Chhe minute chalna rozmarra zindagi ke baare mein bohat si lab tests se zyada batata hai. Test ko har baar bilkul ek hi tareeqe se karna, oxygen aur saans ki tangi dekhna aur rukne ka waqt jaanna seekhein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll prepare and run a standard six-minute walk test, record distance, oxygen saturation, heart rate and the Borg breathlessness score, and decide whether a change is real.
goal.ur: End tak aap standard chhe minute walk test taiyar karenge aur chalayenge, distance, oxygen saturation, heart rate aur Borg saans ki tangi ka score likhenge, aur faisla karenge ke tabdeeli asli hai ya nahi.

text.en: The test asks one simple question: **how far can the patient walk in six minutes at their own pace?** It is a **submaximal** test, so the patient may slow down or rest, and the clock keeps running. Because the result depends on how you run it, the setup must be the same each time: a **straight, flat corridor of 30 metres**, the same instructions and the same **standard encouragement**.
text.ur: Test ek saada sawal poochta hai: **patient apni raftar se chhe minute mein kitna chal sakta hai?** Yeh **submaximal** test hai, is liye patient ruk sakta hai ya aahista ho sakta hai aur ghari chalti rehti hai. Nateeja is par depend karta hai ke aap kaise chalate hain, is liye setup har baar ek jaisa ho: **30 meter ka seedha, hamwar corridor**, wohi hidayat aur wohi **standard hausla afzai**.

text.en: Think of the test as a car road test on the same road each time. If you change the road, the weather or the instructions, you cannot say whether the car got better. In the same way, a change in distance only means something if the corridor, the encouragement, the walking aid and the time of day stay the same.
text.ur: Test ko ek hi sadak par gaari ka road test samjhein. Agar aap sadak, mausam ya hidayat badal dein to nahi keh sakte ke gaari behtar hui. Isi tarah distance mein tabdeeli tabhi maani rakhti hai jab corridor, hausla afzai, chalne ka sahara aur waqt ek jaise rahein.

steps.title: Check before you start
steps.detail: Ask about chest pain, recent heart attack, severe breathlessness at rest, and check resting pulse, blood pressure and oxygen. Do not start if the unit's safety limits are crossed. || Shuru karne se pehle check karein

steps.title: Prepare the patient
steps.detail: Comfortable clothes and shoes, usual walking aid, light meal only, rest sitting for ten minutes. Record the Borg breathlessness score and heart rate at rest. || Patient ko taiyar karein

steps.title: Give the instructions
steps.detail: Say the standard words: walk as far as you can in six minutes; you may slow down, stop and rest, and then start again when able. Use only the standard encouragement each minute. || Hidayat dein

steps.title: Record and compare
steps.detail: Note the total distance, the lowest oxygen, the end Borg score and heart rate, and any stops. Compare with last time, the same conditions, and with the expected value. || Likhein aur muqabla karein

text.en: **Same road, same words.** A six-minute walk result is only as good as how closely you repeated the conditions. Write down the corridor, the aid, the oxygen use and the time of day beside the number.
text.ur: **Wohi sadak, wohi alfaz.** Chhe minute walk ka nateeja utna hi achha hai jitni ek jaisi sharait aap ne dohrayi. Number ke saath corridor, sahara, oxygen ka istemal aur waqt likhein.

text.en: **Walking with the patient and setting the pace.** If you walk beside them, you change their speed. Stand at the end of the corridor, say the standard words and let the patient choose the pace.
text.ur: **Patient ke saath chal kar raftar tay karna.** Agar aap saath chalein to unki raftar badal jati hai. Corridor ke ek sire par khare hon, standard alfaz kahein aur patient ko apni raftar chunne dein.

text.en: **Plan with the number.** Use the distance and Borg score to set exercise intensity: many programmes ask patients to train at a breathlessness of three to four on the Borg scale. Record the same test at the start, mid-point and end so progress is clear to the patient.
text.ur: **Number ke saath plan banayein.** Distance aur Borg score se exercise ki shiddat tay karein: bohat se programmes patient se Borg par teen se chaar ki saans ki tangi par training karwate hain. Shuru, beech aur end mein wohi test likhein taake patient ko progress saaf nazar aaye.

question.en: Why is the six-minute walk test called submaximal?
question.ur: Chhe minute walk test ko submaximal kyun kehte hain?

answer.en: Because the patient chooses their own pace and may slow down or rest, so they usually do not reach their maximum capacity. It mirrors daily activity rather than testing the limit.
answer.ur: Kyunke patient apni raftar khud chunta hai aur aahista ho sakta hai ya ruk sakta hai, is liye aam taur par woh apni adhikatam salahiyat tak nahi pahunchta. Yeh hadd ko jaanchne ke bajaye rozmarra activity ko dikhata hai.

beats.patient: A 62-year-old with COPD walks 310 metres with the Borg score rising from 1 to 5 and oxygen falling from 94 to 90 percent. He stops once for 30 seconds. After eight weeks of exercise he walks 360 metres with a Borg score of 3 and an oxygen low of 92 percent.
beats.assessment: A rise of 50 metres is larger than the change usually needed to be sure it is real, and breathlessness is lower, so the benefit is clear.
beats.treatment: Share the result with him, set training at a breathlessness of three to four and repeat the test in three months.
beats.reassess: At three months he walks 375 metres and manages his shopping without stopping.

text.en: **Do not run the test, or stop it,** for chest pain, a recent heart attack or unstable angina, a resting pulse above 120, a very high resting blood pressure, a very low oxygen reading by your unit's limit, dizziness, faintness, a pale or sweaty patient or severe leg pain. Have a chair, a pulse oximeter and a way to call for help ready.
text.ur: **Test na chalayein, ya rok dein,** seene ke dard, haal ki dil ki bimari ya unstable angina, aaram mein pulse 120 se oopar, bohat zyada aaram ka blood pressure, aap ki unit ki hadd ke mutabiq bohat kam oxygen, chakkar, behoshi jaisi kaifiyat, zard ya paseene mein dooba patient ya shadeed pindli ke dard mein. Kursi, pulse oximeter aur madad bulane ka tareeqa taiyar rakhein.

summary.en: The six-minute walk test measures how far a patient walks at their own pace; it is submaximal and reflects daily life.
summary.ur: Chhe minute walk test napta hai ke patient apni raftar se kitna chalta hai; yeh submaximal hai aur rozmarra zindagi ko dikhata hai.

summary.en: Run it the same way every time: same corridor, same words, same encouragement, and record oxygen, heart rate and the Borg score.
summary.ur: Har baar ek tareeqe se chalayein: wohi corridor, wohi alfaz, wohi hausla afzai, aur oxygen, heart rate aur Borg score likhein.

summary.en: Know the stopping criteria and the size of change that is real (about 30 metres in chronic lung disease); use the result to set exercise intensity.
summary.ur: Rukne ke mayaar aur asli tabdeeli ka size (phephron ki purani bimari mein takreeban 30 meter) jaanein; nateeje se exercise ki shiddat tay karein.
